obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident or funds transfer fraud
deadline: Per policy; call the carrier hotline before engaging any vendor
notify: Carrier breach and claims hotline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal; $10 million funds transfer fraud sublimit

obligation: Recall of a misdirected wire
citation: Fla. Stat. 670.211 (UCC Article 4A cancellation, worked example); FBI IC3 BEC guidance
trigger: A buyer, Title, the brokerage, or Homebuilding sent a wire on fraudulent instructions
deadline: Immediately on discovery. After the receiving bank accepts the payment order, cancellation needs that bank agreement, so minutes matter
notify: The sending bank wire room (the buyer calls their own bank; Treasury calls the group bank for group-sent wires and alerts the receiving bank)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - operational; not a notification duty

obligation: FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) complaint
trigger: Any business email compromise attempt or loss
deadline: As soon as possible (voluntary; no legal deadline). The FBI states IC3 may help banks and law enforcement freeze funds
notify: IC3 at www.ic3.gov with full banking details; the buyer also files
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary; required by POL-03 4.7 the same day

obligation: Parent (third-party agent) notice to each subsidiary whose data it maintains
citation: Fla. Stat. 501.171(6)(a) (worked example); intercompany services agreement (being amended, POAM-013)
trigger: Breach of a system the parent maintains for a subsidiary (SYS-G4 email holds Title, Home Loans, and brokerage data)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred
notify: President, Title; President, Mortgage; Residential Brokerage president (on the bridge, then in writing)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SYS-G4 mailbox incident
notifying_entity: Cris Santos Company Holdings, Inc. (Group CISO)

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule notification event: Title
trigger: Acquisition of unencrypted Title customer information without authorization (unauthorized access is presumed to be acquisition unless reliable evidence shows otherwise) involving at least 500 Title consumers
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 days after discovery. Discovery is the first day the event is known to any employee, officer, or other agent of Title (314.4(j)(2)); the runbook treats the SOC first-knowledge date as Title discovery
notify: FTC through the online form at ftc.gov (six content items in 314.4(j)(1)(i)-(vi))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Title consumers (exercise: 640)
notifying_entity: Cris Santos Title, LLC (President, Title, with the Group General Counsel)

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule notification event: Home Loans
trigger: Acquisition of unencrypted Home Loans customer information without authorization involving at least 500 Home Loans consumers
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 days after discovery (counted separately from Title)
notify: FTC through the online form at ftc.gov
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Home Loans consumers (exercise: 530)
notifying_entity: Cris Santos Home Loans, LLC (President, Mortgage, with the Group General Counsel)

obligation: FTC law enforcement delay request
trigger: A law enforcement official determines in writing that public disclosure would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: The FTC notice is still filed on time; the official may ask the FTC to delay public disclosure for up to 30 days, extendable by up to 60 days on written request
notify: State the determination and the official contact in the FTC notice
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: State breach notice to individuals (Florida worked example)
trigger: Unauthorized access of electronic personal information of Florida residents (for example, name with a Social Security, driver license, or financial account number with its access code; or an email address with a password that permits access to an online account)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
notify: Each affected Florida resident by mail or email (never through the compromised mailbox)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the FTC rule has no individual-notice procedure, so the federal deemed-compliance path does not help; each covered entity notifies its own customers or clients, in coordinated letters
notifying_entity: Each covered entity whose data was involved (Title, Home Loans, Cris Santos Realty)

obligation: Notice to the contractor agent whose credentials were taken
citation: Fla. Stat. 501.171(4) (worked example); personal information includes a user name or email address with a password that permits access to an online account (501.171(1)(g)1.b.)
trigger: The agent mailbox password was captured
deadline: Same as individual notice; the account is reset on Day 0 in any case
notify: The agent (written notice plus the reset)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Florida notice not required after a no-harm determination
trigger: After an appropriate investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the covered entity reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept for at least 5 years and provided to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days after the determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (copy of the determination)
applies_at_this_tier: Possible only for people whose records held no Social Security, ID, or account access data; counsel decides per person

obligation: Florida law enforcement delay
trigger: A law enforcement agency determines in writing that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay individual notice for the period in the written request
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: Notice to the Florida Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida (counted per covered entity)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination. The 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to the individual notice, never to this notice
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (synopsis, count, services offered, copy of the notice, contact)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for any covered entity with 500 or more Florida individuals. Not triggered in the exercise when counted per covered entity (Florida residents: Title 470, Home Loans 410, Realty 300); counsel confirms the counts and may file voluntarily

obligation: Notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a covered entity notifies more than 1,000 at a single time

obligation: Other states breach laws
citation: State breach notification statutes (each state where affected individuals reside)
trigger: Affected individuals who reside outside Florida (exercise: 360 in 4 other states)
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents and, where required, state attorneys general or regulators
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - check the residency of every affected person

obligation: State insurance commissioner notice (Title)
citation: NAIC Model #668 sec. 6 (where enacted; text varies)
trigger: Cybersecurity event involving nonpublic information of Title in a state that has enacted a version of the model
deadline: As promptly as possible and no later than 72 hours after determination, where the state law says so
notify: Insurance commissioner of each adopting state where Title is licensed or where affected residents live (per that state law); Florida has not enacted the model
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - check the Title adopting-state list (POAM-007)
notifying_entity: Cris Santos Title, LLC (Title compliance officer)

obligation: Title insurance underwriter notice
citation: Title agency agreements and closing protection letter terms (contract)
trigger: Loss or suspected loss of funds in a Title closing, or a claim by a buyer, seller, or lender
deadline: Per the agency agreements (treat as same day)
notify: Each affected underwriter agency or claims contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: Outside lender notice
citation: Lender closing instructions and settlement agent agreements (contract)
trigger: Borrower data of an outside lender was in the mailbox, or a funding was affected
deadline: Per each lender agreement
notify: Affected lenders
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if outside lenders data is involved; confirm each agreement

obligation: Loan investor notice (Home Loans)
trigger: Security incident involving data of loans sold to investors
deadline: Per each investor agreement (not verified in this sample; confirm the terms before use)
notify: Affected investors
applies_at_this_tier: Confirm before use

obligation: State mortgage regulator notice (Home Loans)
citation: State mortgage licensing laws and rules (not verified in this sample)
trigger: Security incident at a licensed mortgage lender, where a state requires notice
deadline: Varies; confirm per state before use
notify: State mortgage licensing regulators where required
applies_at_this_tier: Confirm before use; not researched for this sample

obligation: Suspicious activity report decision (Home Loans)
trigger: A transaction of $5,000 or more conducted or attempted by, at, or through Home Loans that it knows or suspects involves fraud
deadline: No later than 30 calendar days after initial detection (up to 60 days if no suspect is identified)
notify: FinCEN (SAR filed by the Home Loans BSA officer)
applies_at_this_tier: Decide case by case: a buyer cash-to-close wire diverted to a mule may not be a transaction through Home Loans; the BSA officer documents the decision (POAM-021)
notifying_entity: Cris Santos Home Loans, LLC (BSA officer)

obligation: Escrow dispute notice to the real estate commission (brokerage deposit)
citation: Fla. Stat. 475.25(1)(d)1.; Fla. Admin. Code r. 61J2-10.032(1) (worked example)
trigger: A diverted or missing earnest money deposit leads to conflicting demands on funds in a brokerage escrow account, or the broker has good-faith doubt about who is entitled to them
deadline: Written notice to the Commission within 15 business days of the last demand or of the doubt; start a settlement procedure within 30 business days
notify: Florida Real Estate Commission (Broker of Record); each state commission under its own rules
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a brokerage escrow deposit is involved (variant A2)
notifying_entity: Cris Santos Realty, LLC (Broker of Record)

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 material cybersecurity incident
trigger: The disclosure committee determines the incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination (delay only on a U.S. Attorney General determination)
notify: SEC and investors (public filing)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the parent is an SEC registrant; disclosure committee decides (exercise: not material, decision documented)
notifying_entity: Cris Santos Company Holdings, Inc. (disclosure committee)

obligation: SEC Reg S-K Item 106 annual disclosure
trigger: Annual report
deadline: With the annual report
notify: SEC and investors
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - consider the incident and lessons in the next description of processes

obligation: Warning to other clients in the compromised mailbox
citation: POL-03 4.7; FTC Act Section 5 (N53-R02) reasonable care (operational)
trigger: Active transactions whose parties corresponded with the compromised mailbox
deadline: Same day as containment
notify: Every buyer and seller with an open transaction in the mailbox (by phone from a verified number and in SYS-B2)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - operational; prevents further losses
notifying_entity: Cris Santos Realty, LLC with Title

obligation: Trade partner and lien follow-up (variant B)
trigger: A Homebuilding payment to a trade partner was diverted after a spoofed bank change
deadline: Before the next payment run
notify: The real trade partner (by a phone number on file); Homebuilding legal for lien exposure
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for variant B

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours; 24 hours after a ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (voluntary until then); recheck when final

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
trigger: Considering an extortion or ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment
notify: OFAC; FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No for business email compromise; applies only if the incident turns into extortion

obligation: FinCEN residential real estate report
trigger: Non-financed transfer of residential real property to an entity or trust
deadline: n/a while vacated
notify: FinCEN
applies_at_this_tier: No - vacated 2026-03-19 (E.D. Tex.); appeal pending; FinCEN website checked 2026-10-06

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered equipment found during federal contract performance
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further report within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the group holds no federal contracts

obligation: Kaspersky covered article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered article found during federal contract performance
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the group holds no federal contracts
